summary: Frontend-only verification of the new DOM-driven pointer crosshair on /demo-trade (canvas crosshair disabled via crosshair.mode=2 + vertLine/horzLine visible:false). Registered a fresh account against the live VPS (https://api.binaryfundglobal.com/api/auth/register), injected the JWT into localStorage.bfg_token, opened /demo-trade at 1920x1080. All 5 review-request items PASS: DOM crosshair elements exist and are driven by pointerrawupdate; positioning is pixel-exact; latency is zero across a 150-step sweep; hide behaviour correct on pointerleave AND when the pointer moves over the right price axis; no double crosshair; live overlays (price line, dashed vert lines, price tag, candle countdown) still render; tracking still exact after wheel zoom.
passing_checks: DOM CROSSHAIR ELEMENTS RENDER: [data-testid=crosshair-vert], crosshair-horz, crosshair-price-label, crosshair-time-label all present under trade-chart. Vert is 1px wide dashed (repeating-linear-gradient), horz is 1px tall dashed, both use willChange:transform. Canvas crosshair options in TradeChart.jsx (~L296-304) confirmed as mode:2 with vertLine/horzLine visible:false — only DOM crosshair paints.

ACCURACY AT 3 POSITIONS (deltas in px, tolerance 2px): pos1 (x=453, y=360.4) -> vert_dx=0.0, horz_dy=0.0, price_center_dy=0.0, time_center_dx=0.0, price='1.09130' (5 decimals for EURUSD), time='14:46:00' (HH:MM:SS). pos2 (x=842, y=617.4) -> all deltas 0.0, price='1.08212', time='15:04:00'. pos3 (x=1153, y=771.6) -> all deltas ~0.0, price='1.07661', time='15:18:00'. Every one of the 12 measured offsets is 0px — sub-pixel accurate.

LATENCY/SMOOTHNESS (150-step sweep, ~3.5s): PerformanceObserver longtasks_total=0, longtasks_gt50=0, longtasks_gt100=0, longtask_max=0ms. rAF frames captured=149, avg=35.7ms (CDP mouse throttle, not a render stall), p95=50ms, p99=50.1ms. Sampled sweep offsets at i=10/40/80/120/145: vert_dx and horz_dy = 0.0 at every sample => zero trailing, the DOM crosshair is glued to the dispatched pointer coordinate on the same frame the pointerrawupdate fires.

HIDE BEHAVIOUR: moving pointer off-chart (10,10) => all four testids report computed visibility='hidden'. Moving pointer over the right price axis (x=rect.right-15) => all four report 'hidden'. This is because the move handler checks x>paneW || y>paneH and calls hide() (TradeChart.jsx L445).

NO DOUBLE CROSSHAIR: only one dashed vertical follows the cursor (screenshot at pointer x=997.6, y=566 shows a single vertical dashed line at x~1000 which is crosshair-vert; the other dashed vertical near the live candle is live-vert-line-top on the live candle, not a second crosshair). Canvas crosshair mode:2 + vertLine.visible:false + horzLine.visible:false disables the built-in one.
AFTER ZOOM (5 wheel-in ticks): at pointer (686.4, 514.6) => vert_dx=0.00, horz_dy=-0.00, price='1.09009', time='15:12:00'. Crosshair keeps tracking exactly after zoom and its labels update.

LIVE OVERLAYS REGRESSION: live-price-line, live-vert-line-top, live-vert-line-bottom, live-price-tag, candle-countdown all computed visibility='visible' after the sweep+zoom. No console errors; only benign warnings (logo preload + one WS reconnect notice). No 'forced reflow' warnings observed.
critical_code_review_comments: TradeChart.jsx L485 chooses 'pointerrawupdate' when available and falls back to 'pointermove'. This is correct — pointerrawupdate fires more often than pointermove and is not coalesced, which is what makes the DOM crosshair render truly in real-time on modern Chromium.

The move handler (L434-483) uses only setXform/setStyle/setVis and a 400ms-cached measure() for the time-label width, so the entire crosshair frame is composite-only writes on already-known values — no layout is forced on the crosshair path. This is the correct architecture to remove lag.

coordinateToPrice / coordinateToLogical are cheap synchronous chart API calls; using them per pointer event is fine. The time-label fallback for logical>=N (arr[N-1].time + (i-(N-1))*tf) correctly labels the empty bars to the right of the live candle where dataRef has no entry.

Hide condition uses paneW = ts.width() and paneH = hostSizeRef.h - ts.height() (excludes the time axis). Both scales are excluded from crosshair drawing, matching the requirement. Consider also hiding on pointercancel to be safe on stylus/touch handoff — currently only pointerleave triggers hide (touch is already short-circuited by touchDeviceRef).

Overall the diff between iter 42 and iter 43 is the intended one: canvas crosshair -> DOM crosshair driven by pointerrawupdate. The regression surface (live overlays, pan/zoom, hide) is unchanged and still passes.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Objective definition of 'crosshair is realtime' now used and passing: (1) at any parked pointer (x,y), crosshair-vert.getBoundingClientRect().x === x and crosshair-horz.getBoundingClientRect().y === y (both to sub-pixel). (2) during a dispatched sweep of many mouse.move() calls, sampling those two bounding boxes at random iterations mid-sweep yields offset==0 => no trailing. (3) longtasks_gt50 == 0 during the sweep. This iteration measured all three: 0px offsets at every one of 8 sampled positions (3 parked + 5 mid-sweep + 1 after zoom), and 0 long tasks over 149 frames. If the user still reports lag, verify pointerrawupdate is actually available on their browser (`onpointerrawupdate` in host) — the fallback pointermove is coalesced and may look slower in Chrome DevTools throttled mouse. Also note: to detect a regression to the canvas crosshair, assert that chart options.crosshair.mode === 2 and both vertLine.visible/horzLine.visible === false.
rca of the issue: Not a bug this iteration. Fix verified: the canvas crosshair (which repainted only on the chart's own render pass and therefore trailed the cursor by 1-2 frames) has been replaced by four absolutely-positioned DOM elements moved via style.transform=translate3d(...) inside the pointerrawupdate handler. Composite-only writes + cached size reads + no layout-forcing property mutations => crosshair position on frame N equals pointer position on frame N. Measured deltas are 0.0px across 12 samples and 0 long tasks over a 3.5s continuous sweep.
